analysis.one_liner: UltraTech Cement is India's largest cement maker (part of the Aditya Birla Group), producing cement, ready-mix concrete and construction chemicals from a capacity base that has swelled past 190 MTPA after recent acquisitions.
analysis.whats_happening: UltraTech reports Q2 FY27 results on October 19, 2026 - just days away - with an earnings call the same evening. The last reported quarter (Q1 FY27, June 2026) showed consolidated revenue up 16% YoY to ₹24,648 crore and net profit up 17% to ~₹2,604 crore, but EBITDA margin slipped from ~21% to ~20.5% as fuel and packaging costs rose. Management has flagged a further ₹130-140/tonne cost headwind for the September quarter.
analysis.plain_terms: This is the company that effectively sets the price floor for cement in India - its scale alone means raw numbers look impressive. The tension is that the stock trades at a rich 37-41x earnings while its return on equity is only around 10%, a fairly ordinary number for that price tag. The market is paying up for continued volume growth and integration of recently acquired plants (India Cements, Kesoram), not for current profitability.
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 (quarter ended June 2026): revenue ₹24,648 crore (+16% YoY), EBITDA ₹5,146 crore (+12% YoY), PAT ~₹2,604 crore (+17% YoY). Domestic cement volumes grew 13.1% to 39.2 million tonnes; ready-mix concrete grew 22% and construction chemicals 52%, though both are small relative to the core cement business. EBITDA margin contracted roughly 50 bps YoY (~21% to ~20.5%) as fuel, raw material and packaging cost inflation offset savings in power and logistics. CFO Atul Daga said the company held per-tonne earnings roughly flat while growing absolute EBITDA 12% despite what he called 'the sharpest imported fuel cost shock in recent memory.' Note: YoY comparisons are partly inorganic - the India Cements and Kesoram acquisitions (completed Dec 2024 and Feb 2025) are still being integrated, with brand conversion at ~58-69% as of late 2025, so quarter-on-quarter volume jumps are not purely like-for-like organic growth.
analysis.performance_read: No stock splits or demergers apply here (has_corporate_action is false), so the price series can be read at face value. Over 3 and 5 years the stock has comfortably beaten both the Nifty and peer Ambuja Cement (5Y: +52% vs Nifty +23% vs peer -11%), but over the last year it has lagged the Nifty slightly (-10.67% vs -9.91%) while still far outperforming the peer (-38%). The stock is down 15.7% from its February 2026 peak of ₹12,791 - this reads as a sector-wide cyclical/cost-pressure correction rather than anything resembling a crash, and it sits above its 52-week low.
analysis.valuation_read: UltraTech trades around 37-41x trailing earnings and roughly 4x book value (figures vary slightly by source - flagged below). It is expensive by any absolute standard. Why it is expensive: unmatched scale (~190+ MTPA), pricing power from industry consolidation, double-digit volume growth guidance, and a track record of successfully digesting acquisitions. Whether it is cheap: not on current numbers - an ROE of ~10% and ROCE in the 12.7-14.5% range are middling for a capital-intensive heavy industrial business carrying this multiple. The premium is a bet on margin recovery and continued market-share gains, not a reflection of today's profitability.
analysis.growth_read: Growth right now is volume-led, not margin-led. Domestic cement volumes rose 13.1% YoY and overseas cement revenue jumped 245% (off a small base), while EBITDA margin actually contracted slightly YoY on cost inflation. That is the more fragile pattern for a commodity business - volumes are climbing but unit profitability is not keeping pace, so earnings growth currently depends on absolute scale rather than pricing/margin expansion.
analysis.health_read: Leverage is low: debt-to-equity is roughly 0.26 and total debt is about ₹19,600 crore against a company of this scale, even as it plans to raise ₹5,000 crore via bonds, likely for capex/refinancing. The board also paid a one-off special dividend of ₹240/share (~₹7,072 crore, the largest in its history) in July 2026 to mark crossing 200 MTPA capacity - this is a special payout, not a new recurring dividend level, and the dividend_ttm figure of ₹240 should not be read as sustainable going forward (the prior year's regular dividend was ₹77.5). The dominant risk here is business risk - cement demand cyclicality and fuel cost swings - not financial/balance-sheet risk.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters (Grasim Industries / Aditya Birla Group) hold about 59.3%, with no pledged shares reported. Mutual funds hold roughly 16% and FIIs roughly 12-13%. Sources disagree meaningfully on the DII (domestic institutional) figure - one shows under 1%, another shows nearly 20% - so that specific number should be treated as Not verified - check on Screener. No single globally famous individual investor is prominently named on the register; this is an institutionally and promoter-held stock rather than one with a marquee retail-investor presence.
strengths: Domestic cement volumes grew 13.1% YoY in Q1 FY27 to 39.2 million tonnes, well ahead of industry average
Debt-to-equity of ~0.26 gives balance sheet room despite large recent acquisitions (India Cements, Kesoram)
Crossed 2 GW of captive green power (48% of power needs), insulating part of its cost base from fuel price swings
Diversification arms growing fast off a small base - ready-mix concrete +22%, construction chemicals +52% YoY
watchpoints: EBITDA margin fell from ~21% to ~20.5% YoY in Q1 FY27 on fuel and packaging inflation, with management guiding to a further ₹130-140/tonne cost headwind in Q2 FY27
ROE of ~10% sits well below the implied return baked into a 37-41x P/E - that gap is the central question for the stock
Stock is down 15.7% from its February 2026 peak, and recent broker commentary includes at least one 'Sell' rating alongside a majority of 'Buy' ratings - a split view worth noting
Integration of India Cements and Kesoram assets is not fully complete (brand conversion ~58-69% as of late 2025), so near-term cost and volume figures still carry integration noise
analysis.one_thing: The Q2 FY27 results on October 19, 2026 will show whether the ₹130-140/tonne fuel and packaging cost headwind management flagged was transient or is becoming structural - that answer determines whether the current rich valuation is justified by margin recovery or not.
analysis.data_notes: Q1 FY27 financials (revenue, EBITDA, PAT, volumes) were cross-checked across Outlook Business, Equitybulls and ScanX and are consistent. Valuation multiples (P/E 36.8x-41.08x) and return ratios (ROCE 12.7% vs 14.55% from different screeners) vary by source and date - reported as ranges rather than a single precise figure. Shareholding DII percentage showed a large discrepancy across sources (under 1% vs ~20%) and is flagged as not independently verified; promoter holding (~59.3%, no pledge) was consistent across sources. Dividend figures are confirmed via multiple sources as a one-off special dividend tied to the 200 MTPA milestone, not a new regular payout level.
